data.name: Georgia
data.summary: Georgia is close to territorial for individuals. Income of a resident that does not have a Georgian source is exempt (Tax Code Art. 82(1)(u)), so foreign dividends and gains on foreign securities are untaxed. Georgian dividends bear a final 5% withholding. Gains on assets held more than two years (not used in business) are exempt; otherwise the rate is 20% (5% for a home or car). Property received as a gift or inheritance by first- and second-line heirs (children included) is exempt. No wealth tax. Residence comes from 183 days in a 12-month period, or by application as a 'high net worth individual'.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Ordinary residence; foreign-source income of resident individuals exempt (Art. 82(1)(u)); Georgian-source income at 20% (5% for dividends/interest).
regimes.eligibility: 183+ days in Georgia in any continuous 12-month period ending in the tax year (Art. 34(2)), or residency granted as a high net worth individual (Art. 34(6)).

capital_gains.summary: Gains from selling assets owned more than two years are exempt unless the asset was used in economic activity (Art. 82(1)(f.c)); merely holding shares for dividends is not economic activity. A home with its land held over two years is exempt (Art. 82(1)(f.a)). Otherwise gains are taxed at 20%, or 5% for a residential apartment/house or vehicle (Art. 81(3)). Gains without a Georgian source (e.g. foreign listed shares, foreign real estate) are exempt for residents (Art. 82(1)(u)).

capital_gains.rate_basis: Held longer than 2 years: Georgian shares and private company shares 0% (Art. 82(1)(f.c)); Georgian residential property 0% (f.a); foreign securities and foreign real estate 0% (non-Georgian source, Art. 82(1)(u)). Within 2 years: 20% (5% residential). Headline = 20% general PIT rate.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Assets used in economic activity do not get the 2-year exemption; frequent trading could be treated as economic activity (no guidance checked).
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: 2 years (Art. 82(1)(f)); holding periods of a parent/testator are added for a first-line heir (Art. 82(4)(a1)).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Non-Georgian-source income of resident individuals exempt (Art. 82(1)(u)).

dividends.summary: Dividends paid by a Georgian company to an individual are taxed at source at 5% (Art. 130(1)), final. Foreign dividends are non-Georgian-source income and exempt for resident individuals (Art. 82(1)(u)).

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic 5% final WHT; foreign 0% because exempt as non-Georgian-source income.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 5% on dividends to non-residents (treaty 0–15%). Companies pay 15% profit tax on distributed profit.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax. Property tax applies to individuals whose annual family income exceeds GEL 40,000 (on real estate, yachts, aircraft, cars) plus land tax.

sources.title: Georgia – Individual – Other taxes

open_questions: Property tax on individuals whose family income exceeds GEL 40,000: secondary sources (Expathub, IBCCS, Revera) give 0.8%-1% of market value above GEL 100,000 of family income and 0.05%-0.2% between GEL 40,000 and 100,000, but the Tax Code chapter on property tax was not opened and the thresholds differ between sources. On a home worth EUR 5m this could be about EUR 40,000-50,000 a year; it is not modelled.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Property tax for families with annual income above GEL 40,000 (rates not stated by PwC; up to about 1% of market value, unverified); separate land tax.

inheritance.summary: No separate inheritance or gift tax. The value of property received as a gift or inheritance by first-line heirs (spouse, children, grandchildren, parents) and second-line heirs (siblings, nieces/nephews) is exempt from income tax (Art. 82(1)(g)). Third and fourth-line heirs are exempt up to GEL 150,000 a year; other gifts above GEL 1,000 are taxable at 20%.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: First/second-line heirs: fully exempt; third/fourth-line: GEL 150,000 a year; others: GEL 1,000 a year.

inheritance.spouse_note: First-line heirs, expressly including the spouse, are exempt from income tax on inherited or gifted property (Tax Code Art. 82(1)(g); first-line heirs defined in Art. 82); there is no separate inheritance tax.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts follow the same exemption (first/second-line heirs fully exempt).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Income-tax based; applies to residents and to Georgian-source property for non-residents.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident for the tax year if physically present 183+ days in any continuous 12-month period ending in that year (Art. 34(2)). Art. 34(6): residency may also be granted to a high net worth individual (as defined in the Law on Securities Market) under rules of the Minister of Finance; Art. 34(6^2) allows other foreigners to be granted residency by the Minister's rules.

routes.name: High net worth individual tax residency (Art. 34(6))
routes.requirements: Status granted on application to a high net worth individual (Art. 34(6) Tax Code; Minister of Finance Order No. 60 of 1 March 2023). Secondary sources (Revera, Eurofast/Mondaq, Expathub; the order itself was not opened) report property above GEL 3 million or income above GEL 200,000 a year for the last three calendar years, plus a link to Georgia (for example Georgian-source income of at least GEL 25,000 or real estate worth USD 500,000), renewed annually. It is a residence status, not a lower tax rate: a family that actually lives in Georgia is resident through the 183-day test and gets the same exemption of foreign-source income.

routes.name: Visa-free stay / residence permit
routes.requirements: EU and US citizens can stay visa-free for long periods (commonly reported as one year; not verified); residence permits on investment in real estate are available (amount not verified).

income.name: Georgia

income_tax.summary: Flat 20% personal income tax on Georgian-source income; residents are exempt on income without a Georgian source. Employees' pension contribution 2% (plus 2% from the employer; self-employed are exempt from mandatory joining); no other social security. Individual entrepreneurs with turnover up to GEL 500,000 can register for small-business status and pay 1% of turnover.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: PwC: from 1 January 2019 pension-scheme membership is mandatory for employees, with self-employed individuals listed as exempt from mandatory joining; if a self-employed person contributes, it is 4% of annual income with a state top-up of 2% (income below GEL 24,000) or 1% (GEL 24,000-60,000), capped at GEL 60,000 of income. The mandatory rate is therefore modelled as 0%; the voluntary 4% is an option. Small-business status: 1% of turnover up to GEL 500,000 (3% above); micro business under GEL 30,000 turnover is exempt.
income_tax.local_tax_note: The pension scheme is the only social contribution; health insurance is not mentioned by PwC. Georgian-source income includes employment in Georgia and services actually rendered in Georgia (Tax Code Art. 104(1)(a), (c), (c.a)); residents are exempt only on income that is not Georgian-source (Art. 82(1)(u)). Residency: 183 days or more in any continuous 12 months (PwC).

regimes.name: Remotely from Georgia
regimes.description: Programme launched in 2020 for remote workers: proof of remote income of USD 2,000 or more a month, health insurance and a clean record, status valid for one year and renewable (CountryTaxCalc). Its status in 2026 is uncertain: another listing says it was deactivated, and no official page could be opened. Citizens of about 95 countries can stay visa-free for 365 days anyway. The programme itself grants no tax relief. Georgia's territorial rule exempts a resident only on income that is not Georgian-source (Tax Code Art. 82(1)(u)), and Art. 104(1) makes income from employment in Georgia and from services actually rendered in Georgia Georgian-source, whoever pays. Remote work done while living in Georgia is therefore taxable (20%, or 1% as a small business), so covers_local_work is false; only income from activity performed abroad is exempt. CountryTaxCalc claims work in Georgia for foreign clients is foreign-sourced, but it is a commercial site that cites no statute.
regimes.duration_note: One year, reported renewable; open-ended in practice with visa-free 365-day stays.

regimes.name: Individual entrepreneur small business status (1%)
regimes.description: Individual entrepreneurs with annual turnover up to GEL 500,000 pay 1% of turnover instead of 20% on profit (3% on turnover above the limit). Per consultancies it applies to Georgian-source activity, which includes services actually rendered in Georgia for foreign clients (Tax Code Art. 104(1)(c.a)); income from services performed abroad is outside Georgian tax anyway. Certain activities (such as consulting, legal, medical, architectural) are reported as excluded and status is lost after two consecutive years above the limit.
regimes.duration_note: Open-ended while turnover stays within the limit.

succession.name: Georgia
succession.summary: Close relatives are guaranteed a share of the estate that a will cannot remove, believed to be half of their intestate share. Georgia has no trust law and is not party to the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations exist as non-commercial entities.
succession.reserved_share: Children, spouse and parents have a compulsory share, believed to be 1/2 of the intestate share; Civil Code of Georgia, art. 1307 (to be confirmed).
succession.foreign_law_note: The 1998 Law on Private International Law governs succession conflicts; whether a foreign national may choose their national law was not confirmed.
succession.trust_note: No trust law. Foundations are non-entrepreneurial legal entities under the Civil Code.

sources.title: Civil Code of Georgia

assumptions: The family are EU citizens who move in and spend 183 days or more a year in Georgia, so they are tax resident under Art. 34(2); EU citizens can stay visa-free for long periods (not verified). The high net worth individual status (Art. 34(6)) is a residence route, not a different tax, and the family does not need it.

Foreign dividends and gains have no Georgian source (issuer and exchange abroad), even when the shares are held through a Georgian bank or broker; how the source rules treat a Georgian custodian was not checked.
Georgian shares are held more than two years and not in an economic activity; the second annual check uses 10% Georgian holdings as the family's real portfolio (90% foreign) would.

No Georgian holding company, foundation or trust is projected: a Georgian company is taxed at 15% on distributed profit and then 5% withholding on the dividend (Art. 97, 98, 130), against nothing for the family personally on foreign income, so it can only cost more. No common local foundation or trust vehicle exists for this purpose.
The property tax on the EUR 5m home (families with income above GEL 40,000) and land tax are not in the checks or the tax file's wealth tax; see the open questions.
open_questions: Property tax on the family home: secondary sources give 0.8%-1% of market value for families with income above GEL 100,000 (0.05%-0.2% between GEL 40,000 and 100,000), which could be EUR 40,000-50,000 a year on a EUR 5m home. The Tax Code property tax chapter was not opened; the tax file records wealth tax as 'none' and the amount is not modelled. Whether foreign-source income counts as family income for the threshold is not settled.
Whether a Georgian-resident individual's gain on foreign shares held through a Georgian broker or custodian keeps its non-Georgian source was not checked.
Art. 130(1) was confirmed on Matsne; Art. 81 (the 20% rate) and Art. 34 were read from the previous research and PwC, not re-opened on 2026-10-16.
The 183-day residency test applies to a family that moves in; the HNWI status thresholds come from secondary sources (Order No. 60 of 2023 not opened).

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary residence)
paths.note: Georgia exempts a resident individual's income that has no Georgian source, including gains (Tax Code Art. 82(1)(u)), so foreign dividends and gains on foreign shares bear no tax. Only dividends paid by Georgian companies bear a final 5% at source; gains on Georgian shares held over 2 years are exempt. Children inherit free of tax as first-line heirs. The home may bear a property tax (not modelled).

immigration.name: Georgia
immigration.summary: Georgia is not in the EU. Citizens of the EU, the US and many other countries can enter without a visa and stay up to one year, so many people never need a permit. Longer-term options are a one-year renewable permit for owning property (now USD 150,000 from 1 March 2026), an investor permit from USD 300,000 giving 5 years, and a remote-worker status. Work permits tie to business turnover.
immigration.naturalisation: Reported 10 years of continuous legal residence with language, history and law tests; the President can grant citizenship for special merit without residence. Secondary sources; statute article not read.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Organic Law: a Georgian citizen may not hold another citizenship except as provided in Article 17; in practice exceptions are granted by presidential decision.

routes.name: Visa-free stay up to one year
routes.summary: Citizens of the EU, US and about 94 other countries can enter on a passport and stay up to a year without a visa. It is not a residence permit and carries no path to permanent residence.
routes.requirements: Passport (EU citizens may use a national ID card); stay up to one year per entry according to travel and news sources. Stricter rules apply to some nationalities from 16 May 2025. Official Ministry of Foreign Affairs list not read.
routes.physical_presence: Up to one year per entry; no residence rights
routes.tax_note: 183 days in a 12-month period makes you tax resident in Georgia (Tax Code art. 34).

routes.name: Temporary residence on real estate (USD 150,000 from 1 March 2026)
routes.summary: Owning Georgian real estate worth at least USD 150,000 gives a one-year renewable temporary residence permit. The limit rose from USD 100,000 on 1 March 2026.
routes.requirements: Property valued at market value of at least USD 150,000 (multiple properties may be combined; appraisal by an accredited appraiser). Applies to applications from 1 March 2026; existing holders renew on the old terms while they keep the property. Spouse and children included. Announced by government document linked on matsne.gov.ge; amendments to the Law on the Legal Status of Aliens passed on 25 June 2026 take effect 1 September 2026 (focus on students and spouses; investor changes not confirmed).
routes.physical_presence: No minimum stated in sources found
routes.family: Spouse and children under the same investment.
routes.tax_note: Permit does not make you tax resident; 183 days does.

routes.name: Investor residence permit (USD 300,000, 5 years)
routes.summary: Investing USD 300,000 in Georgian real estate or a Georgian business gives a five-year permit for the investor, spouse and children, with permanent residence later if conditions are met.
routes.requirements: Investment of at least USD 300,000 (law amendment of 2019 raised it from the earlier level and replaced immediate permanent residence by a 5-year initial permit). Reported turnover tests for the investment: USD 50,000 in year 1, USD 100,000 in year 2, USD 120,000 in years 3 to 5 (OCCRP); not confirmed against the current law. The permit is lost if the qualifying property is resold within the five years.
